alt: A token that only ever moves by +4 or -6, so its position modulo 2 never changes. A target whose difference from the start is odd is ruled out instantly by one remainder; an even difference is always reachable, shown here by the moves +4, -6, +4 closing a difference of 2.

steps.caption: Start at 0, target 2. Every move is +4 or -6, both even, so the position's parity never changes. Check target - start = 2 first.
Move +4: position is 4, still 0 mod 2, exactly as the invariant says it must be.
Move -6: position is -2, still 0 mod 2, exactly as the invariant says it must be.
Move +4: position is 2, still 0 mod 2, exactly as the invariant says it must be.
The position reached 2, the target, using only +4 and -6 moves.
Start at 0, target 5. Every move is +4 or -6, both even, so the position's parity never changes. Check target - start = 5 first.
5 is odd. The position can never change parity, so the target is unreachable, no move sequence needs to be tried.
Start at 10, target 2. Every move is +4 or -6, both even, so the position's parity never changes. Check target - start = -8 first.
Move +4: position is 14, still 0 mod 2, exactly as the invariant says it must be.
Move -6: position is 8, still 0 mod 2, exactly as the invariant says it must be.
Move +4: position is 12, still 0 mod 2, exactly as the invariant says it must be.
Move -6: position is 6, still 0 mod 2, exactly as the invariant says it must be.
Move +4: position is 10, still 0 mod 2, exactly as the invariant says it must be.
Move -6: position is 4, still 0 mod 2, exactly as the invariant says it must be.
Move +4: position is 8, still 0 mod 2, exactly as the invariant says it must be.
Move -6: position is 2, still 0 mod 2, exactly as the invariant says it must be.
The position reached 2, the target, using only +4 and -6 moves.
